restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages M(x), M(y), x != y 256-bit chain values: W0..W7 a constant prefix (a_1 = K9 - K8, a_2 = -K9, a_3..a_8 = 0), W8 = y0, W9 = y1, W(8+k) = y_k - K(8+k) for k = 2..7 (y0..y7 the big-endian words of x). FIPS padding adds a second block: 128 bytes, two blocks, block 2 = padding only, standard IV, steps 0 to 63 on each block, feed-forward, the complete 256-bit digest (sha256-r64-prefix-v1). Found as a collision of the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q, f = walk B of mitchuski's 4684dfc2, an explicit bijection of the block-1 working state after step 63 (proof Section 1): g(x) = g(y) gives equal block-1 states, equal chaining values and equal digests. Plain birthday search with distinguished points; no differential or structural property of the 64 steps is used.

Machine model (the declared prices of this entry's cost model, proof Section 3.1): a classical load/store machine with 256-bit words and 1024 registers (1021 data, 3 pointers) under collision-frontier-v5; 4912 operations (C of sha256-r64) to the unit. Charged, one operation each: every XOR, AND, OR, NOT, set, move, load, store, pointer addition, compare, branch and the random word. A main-loop body record (register-to-register XOR, AND, OR or NOT, no immediate operand) is 5 bytes (an opcode and three 10-bit register fields), the price of dariolina's 6b678689; every other instruction is 36 bytes. The operation ledger is the exact count of the records of the submitted program (86782 per batch, 86819 with stage 1 and the batch loop), listed by `python3 experiments/bssha.py --text` and counted by `--ledger` (proof Appendix A).

time_log2 is an upper bound: every term of proof.md Section 3.4 is enforced by a halt of the program (B batches, e2max stage-1 hits, 62232 table keys, 2 cut trails, one recovery). Recovery pass 1 costs at most capr = c + 2^48 batches; alignment plus the paired loop costs at most capr + 1, including the reachable final evaluation on a false key match, so the ledger charges 2 capr + 1 batches. The attempt is single: one fresh uniform 256-bit word r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, no advice. Distinguished points: low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 941 (density 941 / 2^122). Setup runs the embedded bounded two-pass C emitter: 359452 helper calls and 86782 emitted records at 200 operations each, plus 813600 fixed operations, for 90060400 operations total. The emitted stream has SHA-256 ca25574ff2b094deac1e556a86fd2335887e81e82dde69a4b629121ccd8e645d.

Memory: 62232 table entries of 8 bytes (497856 bytes) plus 496910 bytes of code (86782 body records of 5 bytes = 433910, plus 1750 other instructions of 36 bytes = 63000) plus 16384 bytes of counters, 32768 bytes for the 1024 registers, and 4096 bytes for the recovery array: 1048014 bytes, log2 19.999226558714. The bounded emitter compiles to 4524 WebAssembly instructions (162864 charged bytes) and uses 119529 bytes of fully enumerated scratch, including use counts, input/output state, allocator and CSE state, all 12 mutable u32 globals, 4469 choice bytes, constants and a 4096-byte shadow stack. With the final program, counters, register file and recovery array, setup is 832551 bytes; search is the peak. The claim rounds memory_log2_bytes upward to 19.99922656.

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 of proof.md Section 4 (bounded restart, the detection delay integrated over the remaining batches, the cut count proved; no premise) proves it for a uniformly random function (bound 0.39000, exact certificate 0.390000001000 in Appendix A); H1, score-critical (clauses (a) to (d), declared and not proved), says the real attempt succeeds at least as often. Nothing else in the bound is heuristic. If the hazard were (1 - eps) / N the plan needs extra time: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0762 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2082 bit for eps = 0.25.

The declared experiments run this program in the organizer sandbox: bssha-n16 (one attempt of the 256-lane search per trial on the low 16 bits of the complete digest, DP = low 2 bits zero) and proj-k0-w256 (256 points at width 256 per trial, a pair when two complete digests agree in the low 16 bits). The organizer recomputes the complete two-block digest of every returned pair. They are program checks: no number of the claim is estimated from their counts and no sampling premise is used. No outside code or library is used.

No nonuniform advice; the prefix W0..W7 is a constant of the program, computed in closed form. heuristics.statement: Model premise, four clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds, with the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q (f(x) = walk B, an explicit bijection of the working state after 64 steps of block 1 of the 64-byte message M(x) of proof Section 1, which padding makes two blocks; x the 256-bit chain value; g(x) = g(y) implies equal digests), is at least the probability P_F, over the fresh word r and a uniformly random F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation of g is replaced by F (lazy sampling). Clauses: (a) distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256, uniform and independent outputs; (b) the iterates from r + t have the first-collision law of a random mapping; (c) a point is a distinguished point (low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 941) with probability 941 / 2^122, independently of the collision events; (d) adaptivity: the program chooses its points, and which trails finish, are cut or abort, from earlier outputs of g; given the whole history of the run and which later outputs are distinguished points, a fresh evaluation equals a given earlier non-distinguished output with probability at least 2^-256 (the lazy-sampling hazard of F). Proof.md Section 4 (Lemma 2, bounded restart with the detection delay integrated) proves P_F >= 0.390000001000 for F from the lazy-sampling hazard alone; (d) is the premise that g has that hazard. This is a comparison of two success events, not a statement about the entropy of r. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r64-prefix-v1 restricted to the 64-byte messages M(x) of proof Section 1 (two blocks after padding), the 2^128-scale evaluation of g along about 60300 trails of mean length 2^112.12 started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory: the 64-step SHA-256 map g behaves along the trails of this program as a random function of 256 bits, with collision hazard 1 / N per fresh evaluation; the regime is the 2^128-scale search along trails of mean length 2^112.12. The organizer experiments bssha-n16 and proj-k0-w256 run this program on the real target at reduced width (the search at width 16) and at full width for 256 points with 16-bit projections; they are program checks, the organizer recomputes the complete two-block digest of every returned pair, no number of the claim is estimated from their counts, and no sampling premise is used. Extrapolation from these sizes to width 256 and 2^128 evaluations is by the premise only. If the collision hazard is (1 - eps) / N instead of 1 / N (clause (d), or a deficit eps in clause (a)), the plan of this program needs, to restore 0.39: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0762 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2082 bit for eps = 0.25. Support (proof Section 5): the generic premise of van Oorschot-Wiener parallel collision search, on which this track's generic entries rest (board status review: 3017c952 at round 51, 1884db5b at round 57, 3642e1cd, 6b678689 and 4684dfc2 at round 64, our d4f8f4e4 to 05004d0b at rounds 40 to 53 with this H1); a hazard deficit would separate 64-step SHA-256 from a random function. The reduced-scale observations of proof Section 5 are reproducible observations beside their reference values, not estimates.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about one fixed function, not a theorem: on the target the run is a deterministic function of r. It cannot be tested at width 256; the experiments reach width 16 and 16-bit projections of 256 points per trial and do not measure collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. The bound has no margin above 0.39 (B is the least multiple of 10^24 that reaches it), so any hazard deficit is repaired by extra time, priced above: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01 (Tp 937); 0.0371 bit for eps = 0.05 (Tp 917); 0.0762 bit for eps = 0.10 (Tp 893); 0.2082 bit for eps = 0.25 (Tp 815).
